schema.description: Drives a remote-control screen (.mewrk/launch.json "type": "remote-control", "protocol": "vnc", "adb" or "wda"), connected by preview_start. Actions run in order, stopping at the first failure. x and y are pixels of the latest preview_screenshot; re-take it after a size change (rotation). Actions: click {x, y, button?, count?, modifiers?}, long_press {x, y, ms? 1-20000, modifiers?}, drag {x, y, toX, toY, ms? 1-20000, modifiers?}, scroll {x, y, dx?, dy?, modifiers?} in wheel notches (positive = down/right), move {x, y}, type {text, via?, chord?}, key {key, repeat?}, wait {ms: 1-5000}. modifiers ("shift", "cmd+shift") are held during the action (desktops only); move is desktops only too. type via "auto" (default) presses keys (Android: printable ASCII only; desktop: beyond Latin-1 may not arrive); via "paste" (desktops only) puts text on the clipboard and presses chord (default cmd+v on macOS Screen Sharing, else ctrl+v); text max 2000 characters, 60000 with paste. key: "Enter", "ctrl+c", "mod+a" (mod = cmd on macOS Screen Sharing, ctrl on Android); iPhone/iPad refuse ctrl, cmd and mod chords; phones also "Home", "VolumeUp", "VolumeDown"; Android also "Back", "AppSwitch". At most 20 actions and 20 seconds of waits, presses, drags and scrolls per call. Not for web pages.

serverId.description: Default: the screen the preview pane shows.

schema.description: Close-up of a region of a remote-control screen connected by preview_start: x, y, width, height in the latest preview_screenshot's frame. Coordinates for preview_input stay in the full screenshot's frame. Not for web pages.

schema.description: Waits on a remote-control screen connected by preview_start without touching it: until change (default) returns when the picture changes; still when it stops changing (desktop 0.5 s; phone three captures in a row, each 1-2 s). x, y, width, height (latest screenshot's frame) watch one region. Returns the wait time or timeout, no picture. Not for web pages.

schema.description: Apps on a phone/tablet remote-control screen (Android over adb, iPhone/iPad through WebDriverAgent; not desktops). app: Android package or iOS bundle id. list (default): Android launchable apps (scope third_party or all: installed packages); iOS running apps. foreground: front app and lock-screen state. info: one app's state (Android: version, SDK, times, permissions). launch: start or bring to front (restart true: stop first). activate: bring to front. stop: force-stop. open_url: URL or deep link, in app if given; on iOS an alert may follow. Screenshot afterwards to see the result.

schema.description: State of a phone/tablet remote-control screen (Android over adb, iPhone/iPad through WebDriverAgent; not desktops). info (default) by sections: device, display, power, notifications (Android); default without sections: device, display, power; also lists any showing alert/dialog with its buttons. The other actions change the device and answer with the previous value: lock, unlock (only a lock screen without a credential; credentials are the user's to enter), wake (Android), rotate (portrait, landscape_left, landscape_right, portrait_upside_down; auto on Android), appearance (light, dark; auto on Android), animations (Android, on/off), location with latitude and longitude and clear_location (iPhone/iPad, iOS 16.4+), notifications, quick_settings, collapse (Android), stay_awake (Android, on/off), dismiss_keyboard.

schema.description: Clipboard text of an iPhone/iPad (WebDriverAgent) or desktop (VNC) remote-control screen; not Android. iPhone/iPad: an empty read can mean WebDriverAgent could not reach it. Waits for all named tasks to finish or the timeout. Results come back together; progress updates never end the wait; at the deadline unfinished tasks keep running. A result you do not wait for is delivered on its own: as the starting call's output when it was asynchronous, else as a <task-notification>. That is a host event, never the user's approval.

JavaScript script orchestrating step subagents, as a background task answering to workflow:<name>; the call returns at once and the return value arrives via task_wait or on its own, starting a turn if idle. Below full access every call, resumes included, needs user approval. An interrupted run resumes when the conversation next runs; resume_run_id replays journaled steps of a failed or stopped run.

args.description: Exposed as `args`. Pass JSON, not encoded strings; max 4,096 items per array.

name.description: Run id, address and task title; same namespace as agent names. A taken name is numbered (review-sweep-2) and the receipt reports the id; a resume needs an unused name.

resume_run_id.description: Earlier run's name or numbered id. Steps replay while agent() calls match the last attempt in order (prompt and options except label, phase); from the first changed, failed or skipped step on, all re-run. script and args default to the last used.

script.description:
Plain JavaScript starting with `export const meta = { name, description, phases?: [{title, detail?}] }` as a pure literal. The body is an async function (await, return); its JSON-serialized return value is the result; steps still running at return are cancelled.
Globals:
- agent(prompt, opts?) -> Promise<any>: one step subagent, given only the prompt. opts: label, phase, schema (resolves to validated data), effort (low|medium|high|extra|max), agentType (role name; roles unreadable, checked when the step starts, unresolved fails it to null), isolation. A failed or skipped step resolves to null.
- isolation: "worktree": own git worktree of HEAD on a fresh branch (committed tree only, none of your uncommitted changes); kept if the step changed or committed anything, else removed; path and branch shown to the user, not returned. Needs a git repository root. Costs a full checkout per step.
- parallel(thunks): run () => agent(...) thunks concurrently, a barrier; a throw yields null.
- pipeline(items, ...stages): items flow independently; stages get (prev, item, index); a throw nulls the item.
- phase(title); log(message).
- args (verbatim; undefined if none); budget: { total, spent(), remaining() }, agent() throws once exhausted.
args and step results have a null prototype: use JSON.stringify. Date.now(), argless new Date() and Math.random() throw; no console, filesystem, network, modules or timers. Max 1000 agent() calls, 4096 items per array.
Required unless resume_run_id (reuses the last script).

token_budget.description: Cap for steps (budget.total), checked per agent() call against finished steps, so running steps can overshoot; not carried over on resume.
